 Watch Olivia Dean Have a Full-On, Four-Alarm Freakout Over Her Six Grammy Nominations
 Last year's best new artist winner got lots of love for her The Art of Loving album and massive "Man I Need" single on Monday morning (Nov. 16).
 By
 Gil Kaufman 
 Gil Kaufman

 Olivia Dean at the 68th GRAMMY Awards held at the Crypto.com Arena on Feb. 1, 2026, in Los Angeles. 
 Gilbert Flores/Billboard 
 There are a million ways to react to a six-pack of Grammy nominations. But 99% of them pale in comparison to the unmitigated joy and pure energy that British singer Olivia Dean shouted into the universe when she found out that her 2025 sophomore album, The Art of Loving , and it’s breakout single, “Man I Need,” had racked up a half dozen nods.

 “Ahhhhhhhhhhhh!!!! No Way!!!!!” Dean shouted in the back seat of a car in a TikTok video touting her nominations. “NO WAY!!” she shouted again, slapping her friend on the leg as she (presumably) stared at the news on her phone.

 Dean, 27, was last year’s best new artist Grammy winner and this year’s nominations more than confirm that her first Grammy nom and win to date was no fluke. Dean earned record of the year, song of the year and best pop solo performance for “Man I Need,” which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and No. 1 on the UK singles chart.
 Dean was also nominated for best pop vocal album for The Art of Loving , as well as album of the year and best traditional pop vocal performance for “A Couple Minutes.” The singer will go up against some formidable talent in the album of the year category, which also includes Phoebe Bridgers, Ella Langley, Bruno Mars, RAYE, Olivia Rodrigo, Rosalía and Taylor Swift.
 The singer’s noms came on a morning when women made history at the Grammys , with RAYE tying Beyoncé’s record of 11 nominations for a woman in one year. Additionally, for the first time in Grammy history, the six artists with the most nominations were all women, with RAYE followed by Rosalía‘s nine and Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley and Olivia Rodrigo with seven each.
 The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Feb. 7, with the primetime broadcast airing at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT on ABC and streaming live on Disney+ and Hulu; the Premiere Ceremony, where the majority of the 100 prizes will be handed out, will take place earlier in the day.
